we propose a neural-network architecture for dialogue response generation that models hierarchical structures in the data, that we show that this model improves upon other recent neural-network models, and that the latent stochastic variables in the model help generate long, diverse, and coherent responses that maintain the dialogue state.

1) we propose an end-to-end generative neural network architecture that models complex hierarchical sequential data; 2) we apply the model to the task response generation in dialogues; 3) the model improves upon recently-proposed neural network architectures; 4) the model is able to generate long and diverse meaningful responses; and 5) the model is capable of maintaining the state of the conversation, which is an important property for dialogue systems.

The main takeaway from our work is that
latent variables are useful for modelling sequential data with complex dependencies, and can be easily incorporated into a neural network generative framework.
a hierarchical latent variable model can capture complex temporal dependencies and generate more meaningful responses than recent neural-network-based approaches.
